messages:
mira: Heads up — seeing repeated east-west p95 spikes between GPU nodes in us-west-2a during peak batching windows (approx 09:10–09:20 PDT). Timeline + flame graph: https://grafana.internal/r/ABCD (p95 goes from ~5ms -> 120ms for inter-node RPCs)

jonas: ack, which queues? is it only cross-rack or intra-rack too?

mira: mostly cross-rack (rack-7 -> rack-3) but a few intra-rack blips. Correlates with large continuous-batch traffic (seq len ~1024) and sustained KV cache churn.

sre-bot: incident created: INF-7192 — east-west p95 spike (us-west-2a)

kevin: I pulled tcpdump and RDMA counters on one affected path. No obvious TCP retransmits but NIC shows GRO/GSO flushes skyrocketing. snippet: `GRO flushes: 14823 -> 98214` during the window.

carla: weird, last night’s config push had broad netdev TX coalesce tweaks, could be related. any kernel logs?

kevin: dmesg had a few net_rx softirq backlog warnings. Also saw `eth0: dropped due to skb overrun` on one host.

jonas: could be MTU/PMTU edge-case + RDMA fallback to TCP? When RDMA falls back we get larger skb processing overhead. can we check ib_port and path MTU?

kevin: ibv_devinfo and ibstat look OK, but ib_ipoib stats show some pmtu probes. sample: `pmtu 1500 -> 9000 negotiations inconsistent across TORs`

mira: ops question — did Dedicated autoscaler spin up more GPUs that could have ended up on a different TOR with different MTU settings?

carla: yes, autoscale used rack-affinity loose policy yesterday morning for spill. Some new nodes came from rack-12 (jumbo enabled) -> rack-3 (jumbo not enabled). Could cause IP fragmentation + CPU coalescing pressure.

jonas: quick mitigation we can try: disable GRO/GSO on affected eth pairs to force kernel to process smaller skbs, reduces weird flush spikes. Downsides: more CPU. quick command:

```
# on node
sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off txvlan off rxvlan off
sudo sysctl -w net.core.netdev_max_backlog=5000
```

kevin: also plan B: ensure MTU homogenized (9000) across both TORs and restart rdma service. That’s more invasive.

mira: agreed. let's do a canary first. kevin — can you flip GRO/GSO on two canary GPU hosts in rack-3 during next quiet minute? monitor p95 and CPU.

kevin: will do. scheduling now on host gpu-3-21 and gpu-3-24.

deploy-bot: deploy plan created: INF-7192/mitigation-1 — canary gro disable (2 hosts)

kevin: done on gpu-3-21. immediate observation: p95 for that host path dropped from 118ms -> 12ms during current batching window. cpu usage +8% on NIC CPU.

jonas: promising — suggests offload/coalescing was the amplification vector. can we get per-host socket buffer drops?

kevin: netstat -s shows increased "packets pruned" counters pre-change, now reduced.

carla: opening infra ticket to schedule MTU homogenization and verify TOR configs with networking team. INF-7192 -> INF-7192-NETWORK. I'll own coordination.

mira: good. next steps: 1) extend GRO/GSO disable to affected pool for next 2 hour peak windows, 2) schedule TOR configuration sweep to standardize MTU and offload settings, 3) evaluate RDMA pmtu resilience and add alert for GRO flush spikes.

jonas: also add a fallback routing policy in the serving runtime to prefer intra-rack placement for heavy-batching flows if latency-sensitive. low-cost change.

kevin: will add gro/gso disable script to ops repo so we can rollback quickly. snippet committed.

mira: thanks — monitor dashboards and update INF ticket with graphs. if anything regresses @channel call emergency. :eyes:

sre-bot: patch applied to canary hosts. Monitoring rule: alert if p95 > 60ms for >2 consecutive windows.

carla: noted. I'll ping networking for TOR sweep and file change request.

mira: thanks team. closing loop in a few hours with post-canary metrics.
